clue.text: Do in young boxer? That's planned beforehand

indicators.note: 'in' tells us the musical note goes inside the young dog

parts.note: a young boxer dog is a pup
ut is the old name for the note do in the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: Someone suspects a junior fighter's knockout was a fix arranged in advance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Do in' looks like 'kill'; 'Do' is the note UT and 'boxer' is the dog breed, not a fighter.
explanation.definitionFit: A job arranged in advance, especially a rigged one, is described with this phrase.

clue.text: Seeded player's first love set that put off getting narrowly beaten

parts.note: a fruit with pips, or seeds, can be described as pipped

indicators.note: put off means disturbed or thrown into disorder, so these letters are rearranged
'first' points to the opening letter of the word player's

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, which looks like the letter O

explanation.surface: A tennis seed loses the opening set to love after being distracted, and so loses a close match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put off' scrambles P (from 'player's first'), O and SET THAT into ATTHEPOST. 'Seeded' is not the tennis ranking but 'having pips'.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means beaten at the very last moment, by the smallest margin, as in a horse race.

clue.text: Real ales regularly served? Above all temperature counts

indicators.note: in a down clue the letter sits on top of all the rest
regularly means every other letter of the words real ales is taken

explanation.surface: A pub-goer asks whether proper beer is always on offer, saying chilling it right matters most.
explanation.walkthrough: The even letters of REAL ALES give ELLS, with T placed above.
explanation.definitionFit: To tell is an old sense meaning to count, as a bank teller counts money or votes are told.

clue.text: Sarcastic joke by nice chap

parts.note: a pun is a joke based on word play
a gent is a gentleman, a nice chap

explanation.surface: A cutting quip made by a pleasant man.
explanation.definitionFit: Biting, sharp remarks are called caustic or stinging, the same sense as sarcastic.

clue.text: Make half-hearted attempt to swim in sewer?

definitions.meaning: to act something out mechanically, with no real effort or interest
read literally, travelling through bowel movements, which is what fills a sewer

explanation.surface: Someone half-heartedly tries a revolting dip in the drains.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading takes 'motions' in its medical sense of bowel movements.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes doing something only formally, without commitment or enthusiasm.

clue.text: Complain when terminal's lost bag

indicators.note: the terminal, or final, letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: to gripe is to complain

explanation.surface: A traveller grumbles when their luggage goes missing at the airport terminal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'terminal' suggests an airport, but it means the last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A grip is an old word for a travelling bag or holdall.

clue.text: See 4
Carpeting is semi-fire resistant

indicators.note: semi means half, here the second half of the word fire

parts.note: proof means resistant, as in waterproof

explanation.surface: A floor covering is said to be partly flame-retardant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Carpeting' is not floor covering but a telling-off; 'semi-fire' gives RE.
explanation.definitionFit: Being carpeted means being reprimanded, so a carpeting is a rebuke.

clue.text: United, in sum, on a move?

definitions.text: United, in sum, on a move?

parts.note: U is a common abbreviation for United, as in football club names

indicators.note: move means the letters of in sum on a are shifted into a new order

explanation.surface: A group acting together, all of one mind about a proposal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on a move' shuffles IN SUM ON A into NANIMOUS after U; the whole clue also describes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A body that is united on a motion has every member agreeing with it.

clue.text: Not good — college friend has trashed his accommodation?

indicators.note: trashed means wrecked, so the letters are broken up and rearranged

explanation.surface: A disapproving remark about a student friend who has wrecked his room.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not good' removes G from COLLEGE FRIEND HAS before 'trashed' rearranges what is left.
explanation.definitionFit: Student lodging run by a university or college is a kind of accommodation.

clue.text: Traveller leads Ines a merry dance

indicators.note: leads means comes first, in front of the other piece

parts.note: Marco Polo was the famous Venetian traveller

indicators.note: merry suggests tipsy or jumbled, so the letters of Ines a are rearranged

explanation.surface: A wanderer gives a woman called Ines the runaround.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a merry dance' reads as an idiom, but 'merry' alone is the anagram signal and 'dance' the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A stately Polish processional is a dance in triple time, made famous by Chopin.

clue.text: Maybe conference call finally produces something of value

parts.note: Conference is a well-known British variety of pear, hence 'maybe'

indicators.note: finally picks the last letter of call

explanation.surface: A conference call at last produces something useful.
explanation.walkthrough: Conference is a common pear variety in Britain; the surface wants a business meeting.
explanation.definitionFit: A gem from an oyster is precious, and figuratively anything treasured is this.

clue.text: A problem, delaying time for festival

indicators.note: delaying means pushing the letter later in the word

parts.note: a teaser is a puzzle or problem

explanation.surface: Someone frets that a hitch is holding up the festivities.
explanation.walkthrough: 'delaying' moves the T of TEASER further along, giving EASTER.
explanation.definitionFit: The Christian spring holiday celebrating the resurrection is a religious feast.

clue.text: He composed Ring, creating conflict

parts.note: Alexander Borodin was a Russian composer
a ring is round, shaped like the letter O

explanation.surface: A remark that a composer's Ring cycle caused a row, hinting at Wagner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ring' tempts a thought of Wagner; it is just the letter O.
explanation.definitionFit: The 1812 battle near Moscow between Napoleon and the Russians was a major conflict.

clue.text: You see pronounced assistance stops African country reaching critical situation

indicators.note: stops means plugs, sitting inside the country's name

parts.note: Togo is a West African country

indicators.note: pronounced means the words are sounded out as letters

parts.note: said aloud, you see sounds like the letters U and C
a hand is help or assistance

explanation.surface: Aid to an African nation is cut off as it nears a crisis.
explanation.definitionFit: When an outcome is uncertain and risky, the idiom describes a precarious, critical state.

clue.text: Possibly for a laugh, back independent — or for a stronger reason

indicators.note: possibly signals that the letters may be arranged another way

parts.note: a riot is something hilarious, a real laugh
I abbreviates independent, and back places it at the rear of the word

explanation.surface: A jokey call to support an independent candidate or for some better motive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Possibly' scrambles FOR A and RIOT into AFORTIOR, with I at the back.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin phrase is used to mean with even greater force of argument.

clue.text: Not wanting a certain song that's not on the radio

parts.note: off means not keen on, as in going off something
'the' points to one certain thing, the definite article
an air is a tune or song

explanation.surface: Someone doesn't fancy a particular track that isn't being broadcast.
explanation.definitionFit: A programme or station not broadcasting is said to be this, the opposite of on air.

clue.text: John conceals one in tree stump

indicators.note: conceals means the toilet word covers up the one, taking its place

parts.note: a fir is a conifer tree
I is the Roman numeral one
john is slang for a toilet, as is loo

explanation.surface: A man named John hides something in a tree stump.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stump' looks like part of a tree but is the verb meaning baffle; LOO replaces the I in FIR.
explanation.definitionFit: To floor someone is to baffle or confound them, just as a hard question stumps them.

clue.text: Mother's abandoning dogs as pets

indicators.note: abandoning means leaving out these letters

parts.note: mastiffs are a large breed of dog
ma's means mother's

explanation.surface: Mum is giving up her dogs, which she kept as pets.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pets' looks like animals; it means sulks or fits of pique.
explanation.definitionFit: A pet in the old sense is a fit of sulking, and a minor quarrel or huff is similar.

clue.text: Find out engaging right secretary is better

indicators.note: engaging means taking on, holding inside

parts.note: suss, as in suss out, means find out
a PA, personal assistant, is a secretary

explanation.surface: Discovering that hiring a right-wing secretary works out better.
explanation.definitionFit: To better a rival is to exceed or outdo them, a verbal synonym.

clue.text: Reportedly count on firm securing new agreement

indicators.note: on means following on after the earlier pieces

parts.note: Co is the abbreviation for company, a firm

indicators.note: reportedly means as it is said aloud, giving a sound-alike spelling

parts.note: a census is an official count

explanation.surface: A rumoured headcount relies on a company obtaining a fresh deal.
explanation.definitionFit: General accord reached by a group is shared agreement.

clue.text: Over drug, rising reputation's at issue

indicators.note: in a down clue, the other pieces sit over this one
rising in a down clue means read upwards

parts.note: one's name is one's reputation
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: A worry that a rising reputation is threatened by a drug scandal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'issue' is a verb here, flow out, not a matter in dispute.
explanation.definitionFit: To emerge or flow forth from a source is to issue from it.

clue.text: Present cracking weird tale that's unearthly

indicators.note: cracking means breaking into, going inside
weird means strange, so the letters of tale are rearranged

parts.note: here means present, in attendance

explanation.surface: A gift splits open in a strange story that's otherworldly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Present' looks like a gift but means in attendance; 'weird' scrambles the tale and 'cracking' breaks into it.
explanation.definitionFit: Something airy and otherworldly is heavenly or spiritual, not of this earth.

clue.text: Tunic's flap almost turned grey

parts.note: a tab is a flap

indicators.note: turned means read backwards
almost means losing the final letter

parts.note: drab means dull grey-brown

explanation.surface: A tunic's flap has nearly faded to grey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' trims DRAB to DRA, and 'turned' reverses it to ARD.
explanation.definitionFit: A herald's sleeveless coat, or a sleeveless overgarment, is a type of tunic.

clue.text: Is your setter ready, mate?

parts.note: from the setter's own mouth, is your setter becomes am I
go is readiness, as in all systems go

explanation.surface: The setter asks a friend whether it's time to go.
explanation.walkthrough: Setters refer to themselves as 'your setter', so 'Is your setter' becomes AM I.
explanation.definitionFit: The Spanish word for friend is used in English for a pal or buddy.

clue.text: Gas bill is covered

parts.note: Cl is the chemical symbol for chlorine, a gas
an ad, advertisement, is a bill or poster

explanation.surface: A household's gas bill has been paid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'covered' looks like paid off; it means dressed.
explanation.definitionFit: Being dressed or clothed in something means being covered by it.

clue.text: City in Oklahoma? Hardly!

indicators.note: in tells us the city lies inside the following words

explanation.surface: A quizzer asks whether a city is in Oklahoma and is told certainly not.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is true: the city is in Nebraska, not Oklahoma.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the largest city in Nebraska, in the US Midwest.

clue.text: One's spotted wagging tail and guarding master

indicators.note: guarding means surrounding, holding inside
wagging means moving about, so the letters of tail and are rearranged

parts.note: MA, Master of Arts, abbreviates master

explanation.surface: A dog wags its tail while protecting its owner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wagging' rearranges TAIL AND into DLATIAN, around MA.
explanation.definitionFit: This dog breed is known for its white coat with black spots.

clue.text: Doorstep salesmen initially persist — they're heartless to start with

indicators.note: to start with puts that piece at the very beginning
heartless means the middle letters of they're are removed
initially picks the first letter of salesmen

parts.note: to hold is to persist or keep going, as weather holds

explanation.surface: Door-to-door salesmen keep going, being heartless from the off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartless' takes EY from THEYRE leaving THRE, which 'to start with' places first.
explanation.definitionFit: The strip of wood or stone at the foot of a door is a sill, the same as a doorstep.

clue.text: Aloof, not the first to show strong feelings

indicators.note: not the first means dropping the opening letter

parts.note: remote means aloof, distant

explanation.surface: A distant person is not the first to display emotion.
explanation.definitionFit: To act or express emotion theatrically is to display feelings dramatically.
